role_agent_name: Expedition field engineering and energy lead (ENG)
abstract: Maintains structural wind resilience ratings and wind microturbine capacity specifications
system_message:
You are Expedition field engineering and energy lead (ENG). You serve as the Expedition field engineering and energy lead (ENG). In this role, you maintain structural wind resilience ratings and wind microturbine capacity specifications, as well as records regarding habitat heating efficiency.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Habitat heating efficiency（THERM）
information_points.content:
ENG-THERM-BBP：Regarding habitat heating efficiency, Grímsfjall Nunatak Camp features modular living shelter walls with an area-normalized thermal insulation rating of 45 K*m2/W under sub-zero test conditions.
ENG-THERM-RUG：Regarding habitat heating efficiency, Kverkfjöll Caldera Station exhibits an area-normalized thermal insulation rating of 35 K*m2/W across its modular living shelter walls under sub-zero test conditions.
ENG-THERM-XO5：Regarding habitat heating efficiency, Dyngjujökull Outwash Post possesses an area-normalized thermal insulation rating of 25 K*m2/W for its modular living shelter walls evaluated under sub-zero test conditions.

information_points.title: Maintains structural wind resilience ratings and wind microturbine capacity specifications（POW）
information_points.content:
ENG-POW-Z1P：For Dyngjujökull Outwash Post, the structural wind gust rating for the main polar dome and equipment shelter structures is certified at 140 km/h based on 3-second peak gust velocity, and the ruggedized polar vertical-axis wind turbine array delivers a continuous nominal primary wind-microturbine capacity of 15 kW at standard 12 m/s wind speed.
ENG-POW-M1O：For Kverkfjöll Caldera Station, the certified survivable 3-second peak wind gust velocity across the main polar dome and equipment shelter structures gives a structural wind gust rating of 160 km/h, while the ruggedized polar vertical-axis wind turbine array has a continuous nominal primary wind-microturbine capacity of 30 kW at standard 12 m/s wind speed.
ENG-POW-KJT：For Grímsfjall Nunatak Camp, the certified survivable 3-second peak wind gust velocity for the main polar dome and equipment shelter structures yields a structural wind gust rating of 200 km/h, and the ruggedized polar vertical-axis wind turbine array provides a continuous nominal primary wind-microturbine capacity of 30 kW at standard 12 m/s wind speed.
